why: A classdef object's member written without parentheses calls its method (MATLAB doc 'Method Invocation'), so `obj.level` in a method file of `@widget` calls `@widget/level.m`; an old-style class's object is a struct, and the same `obj.level` reads its field (doc 'Class Folders', old-style classes; matlab-lookup.ts). When `@widget/widget.m` turns from a classdef with a constructor into an old-style constructor, and back, the class keeps every name it defines, and only the kind of object it makes changes: each step must end where a fresh index ends (project rule; step 13). A sync kept `obj.level`'s edge after the turn until step 14, which counts a class whose standing as a classdef changes as one that comes and goes (MatlabSuperclassChange).

known.what: `obj.widget` in `peek.m` links to the constructor while the class is a classdef, and to nothing while it is old-style.
known.why: The resolver's answer for a member read named like the class (a resolution question, step 15); it sits in the case because its edge ends at `widget.m`'s own node, the one shape the classdef flag of step 13's definition delta re-opens by itself.
